claim.statement: The 100 closed disks of radius alpha = 1/sqrt(67) centred at the scaled triangular-lattice sites C cover the closed unit disk D, and alpha is exactly the covering radius of C.
not_claimed: r_D(100) = alpha (no lower bound over arbitrary centre sets)
optimality, local optimality or symmetry reduction
a formalised proof of the infinite-lattice Voronoi tiling

exact_configuration.construction_rule: all sites with i^2+ij+j^2 < 28 (97 sites) plus (-6,4), (-2,-4), (2,4)
exact_configuration.real_position_rule: a*(u, sqrt(3)*v) with u = i+j/2, v = j/2

exact_candidate_radius_argument.lower_bound: the hole point q in D needs radius >= 1/sqrt(3) (normalised) = alpha for any lattice subset

minpoly_checks.irreducibility_method: quadratic with no rational root (rational root theorem)
minpoly_checks.positive_root_uniqueness_method: P(0) = -1 < 0 and P'(t) = 134 t > 0 for t > 0, so P is strictly increasing on [0,inf)
minpoly_checks.scope: minimal polynomial of the candidate covering radius, not of r_D(100)

exterior_sites.reason: cell(p) subset disk(p,1/sqrt(3)) so dist(cell(p),0) >= sqrt(|p|^2)-1/sqrt(3)

finite_reduction.conclusion: a cell meeting the disk has |p|^2 < 29, thus |p|^2 <= 28

negative_controls.expected: cell certificate precondition (cell minimum == target) must fail
negative_controls.detail: cell minimum stays 67/3, so cell((4,2)) meets the enlarged disk in more than the single tangency vertex; the certificate refuses to issue. This is a precondition rejection, NOT a proof that the enlarged disk is uncovered -- covering is monotone in the target radius.

negative_controls.mutation: target disk R'^2 := |x|^2 with x = v + (p-v)/1000, p = (4,2)
negative_controls.expected: explicit point in the enlarged disk outside all 100 disks of radius alpha
negative_controls.detail: x_uv = (9001/2000, 1667/2000), |x|^2 - R^2 = 16001/3000000, nearest centre [3, 2] at squared distance 333667/1000000 > 1/3. This refutes the *modified* claim only; it says nothing about the delivered radius.

negative_controls.expected: explicit uncovered witness: the hole point q
negative_controls.detail: q has real squared norm 1/67 and its nearest configuration centre is at squared distance 1/67 > 1/67 - 1/10^6, so q is uncovered: shows the lower bound direction is live and the delivered radius is minimal.

negative_controls.expected: exactness claim refuted (a strictly smaller radius already covers)
negative_controls.detail: coverage is monotone in the covering radius, so the enlarged value still covers; what fails is exactness: q forces radius >= 1/sqrt(67) and the certified covering works at 1/sqrt(67) < alpha'. No uncovered point is claimed.

negative_controls.mutation: inner product u1u2 + v1v2 instead of u1u2 + 3 v1v2
negative_controls.expected: shell cell minimum must differ from 67/3
negative_controls.detail: min over cell((4,2)) becomes 377/18 != 67/3, so the certificate refuses.

negative_controls.mutation: hexagon vertices rotated by 90 degrees in (u,v)
negative_controls.expected: shell cell minimum must differ from 67/3
negative_controls.detail: min over cell((4,2)) becomes 675/28 != 67/3; the rotated polygon is not a Voronoi cell of this lattice.

negative_controls.expected: shell cell minimum must differ from 67/3
no witness in the configuration -> certificate must fail loudly
negative_controls.detail: the exact tangency neighbours (3,2) and (4,1) lie outside the truncated box, so the certificate cannot be issued: certification depends on the exact neighbour attribution and fails closed.

negative_controls.mutation: claim witnesses {(4,2), (5,2)} for the critical vertex of cell((4,2))
negative_controls.expected: witness must belong to the configuration and lie within 1/sqrt(3)
negative_controls.detail: the shell site (4,2) is itself at squared distance exactly 1/3 from the vertex -- using it (or any non-configuration site) as a covering centre is exactly the error guarded against: [{"site": [4, 2], "in_configuration": false, "squared_distance": "1/3"}, {"site": [5, 2], "in_configuration": false, "squared_distance": "7/3"}]

negative_controls.mutation: configuration := the 98 sites left after deleting (3,2) and (4,1)
negative_controls.expected: coverage must fail with an explicit uncovered witness
negative_controls.detail: the critical vertex (9/2, 5/6) of cell((4,2)) has no covering centre left, so that point is an uncovered witness; shows the coverage test is sensitive to the exact tangency pair.

negative_controls.mutation: drop the three retained norm-28 sites (97 centres)
negative_controls.expected: cardinality check must reject it as the 100-point configuration
negative_controls.detail: the index list has 97 entries, so it is not the delivered 100-point configuration. Note honestly: the 97-site set still covers D at radius alpha (all twelve shell cells, including the three retained ones, have their critical vertex covered by retained neighbours distinct from themselves), so this control rejects the cardinality, not the coverage.

negative_controls.mutation: configuration := the 99 sites left after deleting the shell site (2,4)
negative_controls.expected: cardinality check must reject it; coverage survives (honest labelling)
negative_controls.detail: (1,4) and (2,3) still cover the critical vertex of cell((2,4)) at squared distance exactly 1/3, so coverage survives the deletion and only the cardinality check rejects this variant -- recorded to avoid overclaiming.

negative_controls.mutation: configuration := the 99 sites left after deleting the interior site (3,2)
negative_controls.expected: coverage must fail with an explicit uncovered witness
negative_controls.detail: the site (3,2) itself has |x|^2 = 19 < 67/3 and its nearest remaining centre is at squared distance 1 > 1/3, so it is uncovered: an unselected cell that penetrates the disk (cell minimum below the target) is caught by the certificate.
